chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic
And for the one who fears to stand before his Lord would have two Gardens

He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who knows that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sees him and hears what he says and does, whether from goodness or evil, so that would deter him from the ugly of deeds. So that is the one who fears standing before his Lord, and forbids his self from personal desires.'
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to fear standing before God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) elucidates the verse by defining the fear of standing before Allah as a profound, continuous awareness of His omniscience regarding one's words and deeds, which serves as a spiritual restraint against vice. This concept of *muraqabah* (mindfulness of God) is central to Shia ethical theology, linking internal consciousness directly to the external discipline of the soul (*nafs*) from following base desires. Such divine surveillance acts as the primary mechanism for self-purification, ensuring that the believer's actions align with the expectation of the final reckoning.
